gaps: P0–P1: only manuscript miniatures with court scenes; P2: a single caravanserai, Thelot’s event prints (people, no town) and an imaginary wedding scene, all skipped
notes: #17 comes from Gustave Cirilli’s book on the siege of Adrianople (Gallica); Commons dates it only “before 1914”, but Cirilli was in the city as a correspondent during the 1912–13 siege, so “about 1912” is used. The view shows no visible war damage, so it is not marked as an event; drop it if the reviewer finds the date too loose. #18 (Gadmer 1922, Selimiye at center, nearly the same viewpoint as #17) and #20 (the Meriç bridge in flood, 1922) are good alternatives for P5. #7 (1817 almanac page) is a small vignette probably copied from a 17th-century print, skipped. #9 is Burgas, not Edirne. #11–#15 are Balkan War scenes (burials, guns, troops) with no town view. #21 is the Selimiye interior and #22 a mosque in Istanbul.
